'''Arthur J. Nozik''' (born 1936) is a researcher at the [[National Renewable Energy Lab]] (NREL).<ref name=autobio>{{Cite journal |date=2006-12-01 |title=Autobiography and Scientific History of Arthur J. Nozik |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jp0680948 |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry B |language=en |volume=110 |issue=50 |pages=25126–25132 |doi=10.1021/jp0680948 |pmid=17165953 |issn=1520-6106|last1=Nozik |first1=A. J. |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He is also a professor at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder|University of Colorado]], which is located in [[Boulder, Colorado|Boulder]]. He researches semiconductor quantum dots at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, and is a chemistry professor at the University of Colorado. He also does research for the advancement of solar energy, for which he won the [[International Renewable Energy Agency|Intergovernmental Renewable Energy Organization (IREO)]] Award for Science and Technology in 2009.<ref>[http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2009-06/nrel-nwu061509.php Eureka Alert]</ref>

==Biography==
Dr. Arthur Nozik received his bachelor's degree in [[Chemical engineering|Chemical Engineering]] from the [[Cornell University]] in 1959, and he earned his MS and PhD in [[Physical chemistry|Physical Chemistry]] from [[Yale University]] in 1967. In 1967, he discovered a new [[Transparent conducting film|transparent conductor]] (Cd<sub>2</sub>SnO<sub>4</sub>)<ref>X. Wu, P. Sheldon, T.J. Coutts, D.H. Rose,
and H. Moutinho; [http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.42 ''Application of Cd2SnO4Transparent Conducting Oxides in CdS/CdTe''] Introduction, p2</ref>
Thin-Film Devices, which helped develop new applications for [[solar energy]] devices. Then he did research on quantization effects in [[semiconductor]] [[quantum dot]]s,  for the [[Allied Chemical Corporation]] and the [[American Cyanamid|American Cyanamid Corporation]]. He then worked as a group leader of [[Photoelectrochemistry]] from 1974 to 1978. He worked in both these places until 1978, when he joined the [[National Renewable Energy Laboratory|National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL)]]. He has published a little over 150 research papers related to [[solar cell]], [[quantum dot]], semiconductor, silicon solar cells. He has been an editor of the ''[[Journal of Physical Chemistry]]'' since 1993 and served as senior editor. He has reviewed numerous papers for various scientific magazines.<ref>http://www.nrel.gov/research_fellows/nozik.html {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090826104404/http://nrel.gov/research_fellows/nozik.html |date=2009-08-26 }} National Renewable Energy Laboratory</ref><ref>Nozik, Arthur J. (1996) Martin Karplus Editorial Note, ''J. Phys. Chem.'', 100 (7), pp 2457–2457</ref>

==Career and research==
His research includes the following:
*The effects of size quantization on semiconductor nanocrystals
*The nanostructures of quantum dots, wells and how well they can convert solar photons<ref>[http://www.technologyreview.com/energy/19256/page1/ MIT Technology Review: ''Silicon Nanocrystals for Superefficient Solar Cells'']</ref>
*[[Photoelectrochemistry]] (the study of light through electrochemical systems) of a semiconductor molecule, and their [[Energy transformation|energy conversions]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.compoundsemiconductor.net/csc/news-details.php?cat=news&id=19733499 |title=Compound Semiconductor: ''III-V solar cells turn plants into powerhouses'' |access-date=2011-11-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406161557/http://www.compoundsemiconductor.net/csc/news-details.php?cat=news&id=19733499 |archive-date=2012-04-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[Photocatalysis]], which is the acceleration of a [[Photochemistry|photoreaction]], in the presence of a [[Catalysis|catalyst]]
*Magnetic and electrical properties of solids
